message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study develops an AI-PBPK platform to predict drug fate and tissue distribution, validated against human PK data. However, it does not report on whole, live non-human animals (in vivo) as the index test. The 'in vivo testing' mentioned is part of the traditional process being replaced, and the AI-PBPK approach itself is in silico. Therefore, it does not meet the inclusion criteria for animal model concordance.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study aims to develop an integrated artificial intelligence (AI) and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) platform to rapidly estimate drug in vivo fate based solely on molecular structures.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles and tissue distribution, which are relevant across multiple therapeutic areas rather than a specific one.",
  "model_type": "regulatory-dataset",
  "model_evidence": "The AI-PBPK approach was validated against human PK data of 71 intravenous and 606 oral administrations collected from the PK-DB database.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study describes a computational platform and validation against human data, without specifying or analyzing results from particular animal species.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The AI models were trained to predict eight types of key properties (solubility, pKa values, crystal density, intrinsic dissolution rate, apparent permeability, protein unbound fraction, plasma clearance, and tissue partition coefficients for 15 organs), from which the PBPK model forecasted PK curves."
}
